metadata.title: Data Density Pass 23 -- Day 1 Afternoon Seminary Ridge Final Stand (Ticks 115-145)
metadata.description: The Union I Corps making its last stand on Seminary Ridge before the collapse. Scales and Lane battering the Union line. The breakthrough. Robinson's division trying to hold Oak Ridge. The final retreat through Gettysburg streets. The rearguard that lets the rest escape.

placements.notes: Scales's brigade charging Seminary Ridge -- Scales himself will be wounded. Every field officer becomes a casualty.
Lane's brigade charging north of Scales -- Pender's division's assault on the final Union line
Doubleday's division on Seminary Ridge -- the last Union infantry between Lee and Cemetery Hill
Robinson's division -- they have been fighting for 4 hours
Stevens's Battery B -- firing double canister at 50 yards into Scales's charging men
Cooper's Battery B, 1st PA -- Seminary Ridge artillery last line of defense
Scales's brigade at the Seminary walls -- Scales wounded, every field officer down. 500 casualties already.
Lane's men reaching the Seminary cupola -- Pender's assault crests the ridge
Doubleday's line breaks -- the retreat begins. Ordered or not, they are going to Cemetery Hill.
Robinson's division retreating -- fighting as they go but the line is gone
Stevens limbering under fire -- will lose one gun to the Confederate surge
16th Maine sacrificial rearguard -- ordered to hold while everyone else retreats. They know what this means.
Scales's survivors consolidating at the Seminary
Lane's brigade consolidating -- do they pursue? Hill says yes but then stops.
16th Maine overrun -- 162 survivors from 298. Their sacrifice bought 10 minutes. Worth it.
Doubleday's survivors pouring through Gettysburg streets toward Cemetery Hill
Robinson's men in the streets -- Confederates pursuing to the edge of town
Ramseur's brigade halted -- Rodes orders pursuit but the divisions are disorganized
Doubleday's survivors reaching Cemetery Hill -- forming a ragged line
Robinson's division on Cemetery Hill -- 2400 men became 1300 today
